target.title: fix(config): restrict config paths to own properties
target.body:
Related: #99148

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where config path operations could treat inherited object properties as persisted config. Reads could expose inherited values, unsets could report missing prototype-named keys as deleted, and sets could mutate an inherited plain-object branch instead of creating owned config data.

## Why This Change Was Made

Config path reads, writes, and removals now traverse own properties only. Set operations replace an inherited branch with an owned object, while get and unset stop when a path segment is not owned by the current config object.

This completes the invariant identified by @zenglingbiao in #99148. The original fork disabled maintainer edits, so this replacement preserves the contributor as commit author while covering the full shared helper surface.

## User Impact

Config show/unset behavior is accurate for prototype-named keys, and config mutations cannot follow or alter inherited objects.

## Evidence

- Before: `getConfigValueAtPath()` returned inherited values, `unsetConfigValueAtPath()` returned `true` for missing inherited keys, and `setConfigValueAtPath()` mutated an inherited plain-object parent.
- After: inherited segments are ignored; setters create owned branches without changing the prototype object.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/config/config-paths.test.ts src/config/config-misc.test.ts` — 95 tests passed.
- `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local --stream-engine-output` — clean, no accepted/actionable findings, 0.98 confidence.
- Crabbox `run_9176021d41f4`: `pnpm check:changed` passed for core and core tests, including typecheck, lint, import-cycle, and guard lanes.
- Rebased prepared head: `e526054a6c3` on `d71a24f3a4b`.
